Each marked test function (its extent runs from its marker line to the next marker line or the end of the file) contains every non-blank whitespace-normalised line of its block or the comment `// adapted: <reason>`, declares the app-defined types the block uses (`User`, `UserService`, `Todo` and so on) and runs in `./gradlew build` through the in-memory harness, asserting the outcome that the surrounding docs text states. The `kotlin.md` early-exit blocks run and are asserted: `return@get` yields `404` for an unknown user, `return@use` yields `401` without `Authorization`, and the `if/else` expression form yields the same two outcomes without `return@`. [D-349]

statement: The system shall not use `runBlocking` as an asynchronous adapter: no class of a published module references `kotlinx.coroutines`, no published module has a `kotlinx-coroutines` artifact on its `compileClasspath` or `runtimeClasspath`, and the build check `checkNoCoroutines` fails the build when either appears.
acceptanceCriteria: The build check `checkNoCoroutines`, wired into `check`, scans the main class output of every published module and fails, naming `Class -> kotlinx/coroutines/...`, when a constant-pool class name or descriptor starts with `kotlinx/coroutines/`, and passes on the wave 8 modules. [D-356]

The same check reads the resolved `compileClasspath` and `runtimeClasspath` of every published module and fails, naming the module and artifact, when a `kotlinx-coroutines` artifact is on either. [D-356]

A negative fixture proves both parts as Gradle TestKit builds that need no coroutines artifact from the network: a stub source `kotlinx/coroutines/BuildersKt.java` whose class is referenced from a fixture main class, and a fixture dependency on a `kotlinx-coroutines-core` POM served from a local file repository, each make `checkNoCoroutines` fail naming the class or the artifact, so the check cannot pass vacuously. [D-356]
The wave 1 prefix list of `checkClassReferences` and the pinned strings of `BuildLayoutTest` stay unchanged, and `./gradlew build` passes with both checks. [D-356; CON-BUILD-013]

statement: The system shall write each response through the container's `HttpServletResponse` — `commit` sets the status with `setStatus` and writes each header with `addHeader` in the given order, and `Content-Length` with `setHeader` exactly as the core gave it, without `sendError`, never itself adds, removes or changes `Content-Length` (its own code never calls `setContentLength`; a container may still frame a small buffered body with a length), and returns the container's output stream; `finish` completes the response; `abort` marks the exchange aborted so that every later write, `commit` or `finish` throws `IOException`; `sendFile` writes exactly `length` bytes of the file from `offset` in bounded chunks; and a second start of the same exchange throws `IllegalStateException`.
acceptanceCriteria: A handler's `res.status(201).header("X-A", "1").send("ok")` reaches the client as status `201`, header `X-A: 1` and body `ok` with the `Content-Length` the core set; a `res.stream` response of unknown length arrives with an intact body and without a `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` conflict (chunked framing is asserted only for a body larger than the container's output buffer or after a flush, because a container may buffer a small body and frame it with a length); and no error page of the container appears for a `404` or `500` the core produced, because `sendError` is never called. [D-360]
A HEAD request to a GET route returns the `Content-Length` of the GET body and no body bytes, and a `204` and a `304` carry no body, on the embedded container. [D-360; FR-HTTP-017]

After `abort()` the next body write, `commit` or `finish` throws `IOException` (a write already blocked inside the container ends only by the container's write timeout, FR-SVL-006 AC-3), `abort()` called twice is harmless and `abort()` may run on another thread than the writer; a second `commit`, `sendFile` or `eventStream` on one exchange throws `IllegalStateException`. [r2 W2-006]

`res.file` and `res.download` on a file serve the whole file, a single `Range` (`206` with `Content-Range`) and a `416`, byte for byte equal to the in-memory adapter, with `sendFile` copying in chunks of at most 64 KiB, which a spy output stream records, and never reading the file into memory; the class references no `java.nio.file` type. [D-360; FR-STATIC-010]
Response header order on the wire is the container's, `docs/api/servlet.md` says so, and no test of the shared case suite depends on header order. [r2 W2-006]

With `maxSseStreams(2)` and two open streams, a third request whose handler calls `res.sse()` receives `503` with the standard error body and its request id, because the adapter's counter throws a `503` `HttpException` before the exchange is marked started; after one stream ends a new `res.sse()` is accepted, and the counter is released also when the drain fails with `IOException` and when the exchange is aborted. [D-361; r3 W2-002]

The drain runs on a thread named `naruserve-servlet-sse-<n>` that is a daemon and not a container pool thread, the container request thread has returned from `service()` while the stream is open (a test records both thread ids and the return), and the executor never holds more than `maxSseStreams` threads. [D-361; D-106]

The servlet is registered with `asyncSupported=true`; a test filter in front of the servlet records, after the handler called `res.sse()`, that `request.getAsyncContext().getTimeout()` is `0` for every stream; and a stream kept open longer than the container's default async timeout (the test lowers it to 1 s) still receives a heartbeat after 2.5 s and is not ended by the container. [r4 W2-005]

An event sent from another thread after the handler returned reaches the client within 500 ms of the `send`, a `: ping` heartbeat reaches an idle client within `heartbeatInterval` plus 500 ms, and an event sent by the handler thread before the drain starts reaches the client while the handler still runs, each flushed without further writes behind it. [D-361; D-406; FR-SSE-002]

When the drain ends (client close, `close()` or the core's end report) `AsyncContext.complete()` is called, the stream's `onClose` listeners run once, and `abort()` on an SSE exchange also calls `AsyncContext.complete()`. [D-361; r5 W2-001]

A stream whose client closed its socket is detected by the next write or heartbeat failing with `IOException`, ends with the access-log cause `client` and returns its executor thread within two heartbeat intervals plus 1 s. [D-361; FR-SSE-004]

With one slow plain request in flight, `stop(2, SECONDS)` makes a new request answer `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body at once, returns as soon as the slow request finishes (before the deadline), and a request that outlasts the deadline does not make `stop` return later than the deadline plus 1 s. [D-359; r3 W2-003]

With open SSE streams, `shutdown` delivers the closing notice of FR-SSE-005 through the core, each stream's client sees the end of the chunked body within the shutdown timeout plus the D-344 margin, the `AsyncContext` of each stream is completed, and the executor is shut down. [D-359; FR-SSE-005]

A stream whose client stopped reading is cut at the deadline: `stop` returns within the deadline plus 1 s and the stream's `AsyncContext` is completed, so the container closes the output (Jetty frees a blocked writer at once, another container at its own write timeout, which the test does not wait for); the deviation sentence is present in `docs/api/servlet.md` and `docs/api/sse.md` gains a pointer to it. [r5 W2-001]

`release()` detaches the handler (later requests are answered `503`), `stop` and `release` are idempotent, `stop` before `bind` is harmless, and after `shutdown` returns a test finds no thread named `naruserve-servlet-sse-*` alive within 2 s and no upload temporary file of the app. [D-107; I-015]
Every test of the module that starts the container asserts after shutdown that no server thread and no temporary upload file of that app remains (a shared test rule). [I-015]

The `compileClasspath` of `NaruServe-servlet` main holds `javax.servlet-api:3.1.0` and `javax.websocket-api:1.1` through `compileOnly` only, its main `runtimeClasspath` holds `NaruServe-api` and nothing else, and `BuildLayoutTest` (CON-BUILD-006 AC-1, AC-5) passes unchanged. [D-358]

`org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-servlet`, `jetty-webapp` and `jetty-annotations` at `9.4.58.v20250814`, `project(':NaruServe-gson')` and `testFixtures(project(':NaruServe-api'))` are declared in `testImplementation` of `NaruServe-servlet` only, appear in no main configuration and on no other module's classpath, and no Jetty or Servlet class is on the classpath of `NaruServe-api` or any API 21 module; a build check lists the configurations that contain them. [D-362]

The class-reference check of IR-SVL-001 AC-7 passes for `NaruServe-servlet`, no Gradle module, dependency or class reference for `jakarta.servlet` exists, no API 21 module references `javax/servlet/` (the wave 1 class-reference check passes), and Gson 2.14.0 is the only Gson version on every module's classpath including the Servlet test classpath. [D-358; I-002; I-004; I-005]

The signature comparison test of IR-HTTP-007 AC-4 passes unchanged and removes or changes no public signature of `RestApp`, `Request`, `Response` or `HttpAdapter`; an empty `git diff --stat` of `NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/spi` against the wave 7 merge is recorded as inspection evidence; the TinyHttpd checkout shows no modified file (CON-BUILD-010). [I-006; I-014; D-106]

statement: The release build shall run `./gradlew -Prelease releaseScan`, an OWASP Dependency-Check scan, run in a child Gradle invocation whose exit value is ignored, of the runtime dependencies of the published modules, and write `build/reports/naruserve/vulnerability-scan.md` with the status `completed` and the findings, or, whenever the scanner cannot finish — no network, a missing NVD API key, a rate limit or a tool error — with the status `pending`, the failure reason and the full dependency list (`group:name:version`, one line each, sorted, without duplicates), without failing the build for that reason.
rationale: Covers D-376, wave decision Release scan and result rows (r3 W2-005: pending for any reason the scanner cannot finish) and T50; the block on findings is FR-REL-003. Measured (2026-10-20): the Gradle plugin portal lists `org.owasp:dependency-check-gradle` up to 13.0.0; the network was reachable but a scan without an NVD API key is rate-limited and can fail partway; the shipped runtime dependencies are Gson 2.14.0 with `com.google.errorprone:error_prone_annotations:2.48.0`, `kotlin-stdlib` 2.2.0 with `org.jetbrains:annotations:13.0`, `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 and the TinyHttpd components, as `build/reports/naruserve/dependency-graphs.txt` lists them per module and configuration. Decision: the pure parts — the report writer, the pending decision and the dependency-list derivation — are plain Java 8 sources in `gradle/release-tools` (package `com.snoworca.naruserve.release`), which the root `test` source set adds as a source directory (so the unit tests compile in the default build) and which `gradle/release.gradle` compiles with its own `JavaCompile` task and runs with `JavaExec` tasks, so the script never needs compiled classes at configuration time, so the default build can test them without any plugin or network. Decision: the committed record of the release run is `docs/release/vulnerability-scan.md`, copied from the build report; the scan covers the `runtimeClasspath` of the nine published modules and excludes test scope (Jetty 9.4 of the Servlet tests); the scanner's own failure is caught by a wrapper task that writes the pending report. Measured by prototype (2026-10-20, feasibility run): Dependency-Check 13.0.0 aborts with "Analysis failed" even with `failOnError=false`, so a failure inside the same build cannot be turned into a record; `releaseScan` therefore runs the scan in a child Gradle invocation with `ignoreExitValue` and writes `pending` on a non-zero exit or a missing report. Pitfall: Dependency-Check fails the build on an update error by default; the wrapper converts that into `pending`, otherwise an offline release machine could not record anything. Rejected alternative: treating a pending scan as a pass; the record says `pending`, T50 stays `manual-pending` for this part and I-020 forbids promoting a requirement on a pending check.
acceptanceCriteria: With the scanner stubbed to fail for each of four causes — no network, a missing NVD API key, a rate limit and a tool error — the report writer in `gradle/release-tools` produces a report whose status line is `pending`, whose reason line names the cause, and whose dependency list equals the sorted union of the `group:name:version` of the `runtimeClasspath` entries of the nine published modules in `dependency-graphs.txt` without the project's own `com.snoworca.naruserve:*` components and with the `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd` components kept, which a default-build test over the writer asserts without network. [D-376; r3 W2-005]

A finished scan produces the status `completed` with a findings table (dependency, identifier, CVSS score, severity), or the sentence `no findings`, and the report names the scanner version and the data timestamp. [D-376]

`docs/release/vulnerability-scan.md` exists and holds the report of the release run (`pending` with the reason, or `completed`), and the T50 vulnerability line of `docs/release/test-results.md` is `manual-pending` when the report is `pending` and `verified` when it is `completed` on the release machine, which a docs test compares. [D-376; D-381]
The report's dependency list excludes `compileOnly` and test-scope artifacts (the Servlet API, JSpecify, JUnit, Jetty) and includes the TinyHttpd components. [D-376]

`releaseScan` runs the scanner in a child Gradle invocation with `ignoreExitValue` and writes the `pending` report when that invocation exits non-zero or leaves no report file, which the report writer's test covers with a stub exit code. [D-376; r3 W2-005]

rationale: Covers D-378 and T50. Measured (2026-10-20): the root `LICENSE` and `/Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/LICENSE` both open "BSD 3-Clause License"; Gson, `com.google.errorprone:error_prone_annotations:2.48.0` (Gson's transitive dependency), `kotlin-stdlib` and `org.jetbrains:annotations:13.0` are Apache-2.0 and `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 is MIT by their POMs; `javax.servlet-api` 3.1.0 (CDDL with GPLv2 classpath exception) is `compileOnly` and therefore provided by the container, not shipped; `build.gradle` already writes the resolved graphs to `build/reports/naruserve/dependency-graphs.txt` (`checkDependencyRules`). Decision: licenses come from the POMs through an artifact resolution query; the TinyHttpd components come from an override table in `gradle/release.gradle` with the source `TinyHttpd/LICENSE` (the included build has no POM); a component with no license information and no override fails the task; the file also lists the compile-only artifacts under "provided by the container or the build, not shipped" with their licenses so the CDDL/GPL entry is explicit. Pitfall: the `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 POM has no `<licenses>` element; its MIT license is declared in the parent POM, so the resolution walks the parent POM chain before it reports a missing license. Pitfall: a dependency whose POM states two licenses (dual license) passes when at least one is non-GPL and the file lists both. Rejected alternative: a name-based allowlist of group ids; a new transitive dependency would pass unseen.
acceptanceCriteria: `releaseLicenses` writes `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` with one row per shipped dependency taken from the `runtimeClasspath` entries of `dependency-graphs.txt` — Gson 2.14.0, `error_prone_annotations` 2.48.0, `kotlin-stdlib` 2.2.0, `org.jetbrains:annotations` 13.0, `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 and the TinyHttpd components — giving license name and URL, and a section of provided artifacts that names `javax.servlet-api` as container-provided and not shipped. [D-378; T50]

The license check, exercised by a default-build test over its decision function in `gradle/release-tools` with fixtures, fails for GPL-2.0, LGPL-3.0 and AGPL-3.0 and for an unknown license after the parent POM chain was searched (a license declared only in a parent POM counts), and passes for Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-3-Clause and a dual license with one non-GPL member. [D-378]

A default-build test compares the dependency list parsed from the `runtimeClasspath` entries of `build/reports/naruserve/dependency-graphs.txt` (without the project's own `com.snoworca.naruserve:*` components, with the `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd` components kept) with the rows of `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and fails, naming the dependency, on a missing or extra row, so the committed file cannot go stale. [D-378; I-005]
The run of `releaseLicenses` on the release machine is recorded under T50 in `docs/release/test-results.md` with its command and result. [D-378; D-381]

The document has one line for each of T01 to T50, a second line for T26 and T49 and three lines for T50, so 54 lines in all, whose test ids equal the ids of the §17.2 table of `object.md`, which a docs test parses from both files. [D-381; I-018]

Each line carries exactly one of the literals `automated` (an automated test of the default `./gradlew build` covers it), `manual-pending` (a run or check that has not happened yet), `verified` (a run on the release machine or a manual check with recorded evidence) and `out-of-v1-scope`, and the test rejects any other status word; the platform matrix of OPS-REL-004 and the scan report of FR-REL-002 use the word `pending` of D-376 and D-382 for a run that has not happened, which corresponds to the literal `manual-pending` in this document; T10, T12, T47, the T26 device line and the T49 device line carry `out-of-v1-scope` with the reason `user decision 2026-10-20`, and no other line carries it. [D-381; r1 W1-001; r2 W2-005; r3 W2-005]

Each `automated` line links a test file that exists, and when the link has a `#method` part the method exists in that file; each `manual-pending` line links a checklist item of the document; each `verified` line links the recorded evidence of a run with its command and date; the three T50 lines link their records (the SBOM run and the license run `verified` when a `-Prelease` run on the release machine is recorded and `manual-pending` otherwise, and the vulnerability scan record `manual-pending` when its status is `pending` and `verified` when `completed`). [D-381; I-018]

The document contains, in a separate "Post-v1 items" section outside the 54 status lines, a row for the low-end Android tuning of D-347, and records the date, command, commit and test count of the full-suite run of `./gradlew build` (I-019); no requirement is `verified` on the strength of a `manual-pending` line (I-020). [D-347; I-019; I-020]

`docs/release/test-results.md` states, as `README.md` does, that the Android sample build and API 21 device or emulator verification are not part of v1 and that API 21 compatibility rests on `--release 8` and the animal-sniffer `android-api-level-21` check. [r1 W1-005; D-381]

rationale: Covers D-375, wave decision Release plugins (r4 W2-004), I-019 and T50. Measured (2026-10-20): the nine published modules are the entries of `naruModules` in `build.gradle:11-12`; the Gradle plugin portal metadata lists `org.cyclonedx:cyclonedx-gradle-plugin` up to 3.5.1 and the network was reachable; `build.gradle` has a `plugins {}` block with `ru.vyarus.animalsniffer` and the Kotlin plugin `apply false`. Decision: the plugin is applied from `gradle/release.gradle`, a script plugin with its own `buildscript {}` block, because a `plugins {}` block cannot be conditional and resolves its plugin even with `apply false`; `gradle/release.gradle` is not a module build file, so CON-BUILD-017 AC-2 (no `build.gradle` in a module directory) holds; CON-BUILD-003 AC-1 (the root `build.gradle` holds every module's configuration) would read false once release tasks live in the applied script, so wave 8 supersedes CON-BUILD-003 with CON-BUILD-017, whose AC-1 states the one exception, and the line of `CLAUDE.md` that says the root `build.gradle` configures all modules gets the same exception sentence. The plugin version is an exact literal pinned when the file is written (not a dynamic range); the SBOM files go to `build/reports/naruserve/sbom/<module>.cdx.json`; the lifecycle task names are `releaseSbom`, `releaseScan`, `releaseLicenses` and `releaseCheck`. Pitfall: `BuildLayoutTest` reads `build.gradle` for pinned strings (`'java-library'`, `options.release = 8`, the class-reference prefixes), so the conditional apply is added without touching them. Measured by prototype (2026-10-20, feasibility run): applying the CycloneDX plugin by id from a subproject failed while applying it by class (`org.cyclonedx.gradle.CyclonedxPlugin`) from the script plugin wrote nine SBOMs including the TinyHttpd components. Rejected alternative: a `buildscript { classpath }` in the root file; it resolves the plugin on every build, including offline.
